chain.label: First officer very inexperienced in type and flying the approach
chain.trigger: the first officer had accumulated ... about 20 hours of which were with the company as first officer in its ATR-42 and -72 airplanes ... Flight 5401 was the first officer's first scheduled flight since he completed IOE

chain.label: Airline had no bounced landing recovery guidance or training
chain.trigger: the company did not provide formalized bounced landing recovery techniques to pilots before the accident and ... none of the company manuals contained any information about bounced landing recovery

chain.label: Preexisting weld discontinuities in captain seat sleeve/end-cap joints
chain.trigger: the presence of dark, oxidized, preexisting regions that were consistent with weld discontinuities at the inner diameter side of both joints ... consistent with a lack of fusion

chain.label: Approach airspeed procedure not followed; threshold crossed about 15 knots fast
chain.trigger: the flight crewmembers did not account for winds when calculating the Vref ... the airplane crossed the runway threshold at an airspeed of about 110 KIAS, which was almost 15 knots more than the Vref set on both pilots' airspeed indicators (96 KIAS)

chain.label: Airplane ballooned, touched down long and skipped back into the air
chain.trigger: the airplane touched down on the runway the first time about 1449:41 and then skipped and became airborne, reaching an altitude of about 4 feet

caused_by.evidence: A skip or a bounce is typically caused by excessive airspeed or excessive back pressure being applied to the flight controls by the pilot
the captain stated, 'you're ballooning,' and the first officer replied, 'all right'

chain.label: Captain took control of the airplane during the landing sequence
chain.trigger: At 1449:41, the captain stated, 'get the power,' and, 1 second later, 'my aircraft.' The first officer responded, 'your airplane.'

caused_by.evidence: After the initial touchdown, the captain took control of the airplane
the captain took control of the airplane, most likely because of the first officer's inexperience

chain.label: Captain's abrupt pitch and power inputs instead of proper bounce recovery
chain.trigger: FDR data indicated that he then made several abrupt changes in pitch and power ... the captain's actions after the initial touchdown resulted in the airplane bouncing on the runway twice

caused_by.evidence: After the initial touchdown, the captain took control of the airplane ... he then made several abrupt changes in pitch and power
written company guidance on bounced landing recovery techniques would have increased the possibility that the captain could have recovered from the bounced landings

chain.label: Captain did not execute a go-around after the bounces
chain.trigger: after each bounce of the airplane on the runway, the captain did not make appropriate pitch and power corrections or execute a go-around, both of which were causal to the accident

caused_by.evidence: The captain's inputs made it less likely that he could recover from the two bounces and safely land the airplane; as a result, he should have executed a go-around
written company guidance ... would have increased the possibility that the captain could have ... handled the airplane more appropriately by executing a go-around

chain.label: Third touchdown at descent rate and loads far beyond design limits
chain.trigger: the FDR recorded vertical and lateral loads of about 5 Gs and 0.85 G ... The airplane's descent rate was determined to be about 19 to 32 fps

caused_by.evidence: the captain's actions after the initial touchdown resulted in the airplane bouncing on the runway twice
his subsequent failure to execute a go-around

chain.label: Left main landing gear trunnion fractured in overload
chain.trigger: the airplane's third touchdown severely damaged the left MLG, which caused it to fracture circumferentially at its vertical trunnion leg just below the actuator attach point

caused_by.evidence: the vertical forces on the left MLG exceeded those that the gear was designed to withstand, and these excessive forces resulted in overload failure

chain.label: Captain's cockpit seat failed under the touchdown loads
chain.trigger: at some point during the accident sequence, the captain cockpit seat failed when it was subjected to vertical loads that exceeded those required for certification

caused_by.evidence: The average vertical load for the left side of the cockpit area was calculated to be about 12 Gs
the weld that attached the end cap to the sleeve was fractured at both welded joints ... the accident end cap and sleeve assemblies did not meet manufacturing specifications

chain.label: Airplane departed the left side of runway 8 onto the grass
chain.trigger: Evidence of another ground impact (from the airplane's fourth touchdown) was found on the grassy area about 145 feet left of the runway 8 centerline

caused_by.evidence: the left MLG ... fracture circumferentially at its vertical trunnion leg
the airplane touched down a fourth time ... it was banked 29 degrees left wing down

chain.label: Airplane crashed and was substantially damaged
chain.trigger: left wing tip scrape marks, left engine propeller strike marks, and a fuselage belly impact impression ... The airplane was substantially damaged.

caused_by.evidence: The main wreckage was located about 217 feet left of the runway 8 centerline and about 4,317 beyond the runway threshold
the captain's failure to execute proper techniques to recover from the bounced landings and his subsequent failure to execute a go-around

chain.label: Captain seriously injured; 19 other occupants minor injuries
chain.trigger: The captain was seriously injured; the first officer, 2 flight attendants, and 16 of the 22 passengers received minor injuries

caused_by.evidence: skipped once, bounced hard twice, and then crashed at Luis Munoz Marin International Airport
